verdict.label: contradictory
verdict.rationale: Both cross-sectional studies assess the association between circulating adiponectin and HbA1c. Study A (168 perimenopausal women) reports that adiponectin negatively correlated with HbA1C, while study B (173 patients with type-2 DM) reports a positive correlation with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032). The directions are genuinely opposite. No contextual difference stated in either abstract (population, design, or analysis) is offered as an explanation for the opposing direction, so the pair is contradictory.

source_evidence.quote: Adiponectin negatively correlated with HbA1C, fasting blood glucose, insulin, and triglycerides.

Adiponectin was negatively correlated with waist circumference (r = -0.16, P = 0.06) and positively with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032), total cholesterol (r = 0.23, P = 0.017), LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), SD-LDL (r = 0.41, P < 0.001), and SD-LDL/LDL (r = 0.22, P = 0.023).

diagnostics.notes: Extraction on both sides matches the source text: A extracts a negative adiponectin-HbA1C association; B extracts a positive association (r = 0.19, P = 0.032). Both are cross-sectional correlation analyses without reported adjustment. Populations differ (perimenopausal women vs type-2 DM patients), but neither abstract provides a text-supported explanation for the opposite directions.
